title: Size of the strict w-local construction
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\kappa$ an infinite cardinal with $|A|\leq\kappa$. Let $C_A$ be the algebra defined by the strict w-local construction [def-weil-pbc-strict-w-cover], namely $W=A^w$, $E=W^{\mathrm e}$, and $C_A=E_{[V(IE)]}$ where $I$ is the radical ideal defining the closed points of $\operatorname{Spec}W$. Then $|C_A|\leq\kappa$.

source.place: Tag 0976, remark-size-w; Tag 097S, remark-size-T; Tag 0984, remark-size-w-contractible, the estimates for the first three stages only; Tag 097X, lemma-get-w-local-algebraic-residue-field-extensions, first paragraph of proof specifying these stages

proof.text: Fix a set $K$ of cardinality $\kappa$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-list-cardinality], finite lists in $K$, and any fixed finite iteration of the list construction, have cardinality at most $\kappa$. We will encode finite data by such nested lists: elements of a set of size at most $\kappa$ are injected into $K$, natural numbers are encoded by lengths of lists of a fixed element of $K$, and a tuple or a tagged expression is encoded as a list of its fields. Subsets and images of these code sets have size at most $\kappa$ (choose one preimage for each element of an image). In particular, a family with at most $\kappa$ indices and at most $\kappa$ elements in each member has a disjoint union of size at most $\kappa$: encode an index and an element by a two-field list.

source.place: Tags 0976 (remark-size-w), 097S (remark-size-T); their reference to Sets Tag 000D

proof.text: For any ring $R$ with $|R|\leq\kappa$, constructible subsets in [def-weil-pbc-w-local] are finite Boolean expressions in $D(f)$ and $V(f)$, $f\in R$. Encode each expression by its finite syntax and coefficients in $R$, using step 1. There are at most $\kappa$ such subsets, hence at most $\kappa$ finite partitions with chosen denominators $(f_E)$ in [def-weil-pbc-w-localization]. No counting of all subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is used. These indices form a set and are directed by the common-refinement rule in the definition.

source.place: Tag 0976, remark-size-w; adaptation to the finite-constructible-partition definition

proof.text: At an index $(\mathcal P,(f_E))$, every element of $\prod_{E\in\mathcal P}R_{f_E}$ is a finite tuple of fractions $a_E/f_E^{n_E}$, so its elements are images of finite codes in $R$ and $\mathbf N$ and have size at most $\kappa$ by step 1. Apply [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](1) to the small directed ring diagram of [def-weil-pbc-w-localization]: every element of $R^w$ is represented in one stage. The index-element codes of steps 1 and 2 therefore surject onto $R^w$, giving $|R^w|\leq\kappa$. This argument is valid for every $R$ of the stated size, and in particular gives $|W|=|A^w|\leq\kappa$.

For a ring $R$ of size at most $\kappa$, by [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], a finitely presented $R$-algebra means an algebra isomorphic to $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ for finite $n,m$ and polynomials $g_j$. A polynomial is a finite sum of monomials, each given by a coefficient in $R$ and a finite list of natural-number exponents. Thus the presentations and their polynomial elements admit finite nested-list codes as in step 1. There are at most $\kappa$ isomorphism classes of finitely presented $R$-algebras, and each such algebra has at most $\kappa$ elements. Restricting to the faithfully flat etale algebras selected in [def-weil-pbc-etale-contraction] only decreases the number of classes. One representative per isomorphism class is essential here; arbitrary isomorphic copies are not counted.

source.place: Tag 097S, remark-size-T; section-construction-ind-etale, finite polynomial presentations

proof.text: Consider one successor stage of [def-weil-pbc-etale-contraction] over $R$ of size at most $\kappa$. Its index set consists of finite subsets of the representative set from step 4, hence has size at most $\kappa$ by step 1. A finite tensor product of the representatives has the polynomial presentation obtained by concatenating their finite variable lists and imposing their respective relation lists in that polynomial ring: maps from this quotient to a commutative $R$-algebra are exactly families of maps from the factors. It therefore has size at most $\kappa$ by step 4, including the empty tensor product $R$. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](1), every element of the filtered colimit of these finite tensor products is represented at one finite subset. The index-element encoding of step 1 bounds this successor stage by $\kappa$.

For the sequence $R_0=W$, $R_{n+1}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-contraction], induction gives $|R_n|\leq\kappa$: the base is step 3 and the successor is step 5. The category $\mathbf N$ is small and directed. Apply [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](1) to represent every element of $E=W^{\mathrm e}=\varinjlim_nR_n$ by a pair $(n,a)$, $a\in R_n$. Encoding the natural-number index and the element by step 1 gives $|E|\leq\kappa$.

source.place: Tag 097S, remark-size-T, final sentence on the countable iteration

proof.text: Put $T=V(IE)\subset\operatorname{Spec}E$, which is closed by the definition of an ideal zero locus. Apply the general bound of step 3 again with $R=E$ to obtain $|E^w|\leq\kappa$. The constructible neighbourhoods of $T$ are a subfamily of the constructible subsets counted in step 2, hence form a set of size at most $\kappa$. They are nonempty as an indexing family (the whole spectrum is a neighbourhood) and directed in reverse inclusion by finite intersection, as stipulated in [def-weil-pbc-retained-localization]. Each $(E^w)_{e_U}$ has at most $\kappa$ elements: its fractions $b/e_U^n$ are finite codes in $E^w$ and $\mathbf N$. By [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise](1), each element of their colimit is represented at one neighbourhood. The index-element encoding of step 1 bounds that colimit by $\kappa$. By [def-weil-pbc-strict-w-cover], it is exactly $E_{[V(IE)]}=C_A$, proving the assertion.
